title: MeRIP-Seq/m6A-seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic for the grouped MeRIP-Seq/m6A-seq family: RNA extraction, RNA shortening, m6A-directed immunoprecipitation, and reverse transcription to the drawn cDNA endpoint. A broad sequencing-library/sequencing continuation is supported by the catalogue and MeRIP full text, not depicted as a separate panel. The two publication-associated method names are retained separately; the schematic does not establish identical implementations or a development relationship. The RBP/chromatin-like cartoons are context, with no extra assay branch.

features: The repeated workflow-start vignette labels Methylated RNA and RBP; purple RNA bears small red marks, beside a blue RBP icon and gray chromatin-like drawings.
The leftmost copy accompanies the method title, rather than depicting a separate material route. No RBP immunoprecipitation or crosslinking operation is shown.

states.label: cDNA representing the selected RNA fragments
features: Three black strands labeled cDNA are the final depicted material; red modification marks are absent.

cDNA carries sequence identity from the selected RNA. Its membership in the enriched fraction provides the association with candidate m6A-containing RNA, rather than copying the RNA methyl group as a methylation-specific sequence code.
No adapters, barcodes, strand orientation, or single-/double-stranded library structure are specified.

evidence.locator: Rightmost endpoint: three black strands above cDNA label

evidence.quote: MeRIP-Seq maps m6A-methylated RNA. In this method, m6A-specific antibodies are used to immunoprecipitate RNA. RNA is reverse-transcribed to cDNA and sequenced.
Because methylation of adenosine does not alter its ability to base pair with thymidine or uracil, m6A is not amenable to detection with standard hybridization or sequencing-based methods.
evidence.rationale: Together with the diagrammed reverse transcription to unmarked cDNA, this supports interpreting DNA sequence as the carrier of fragment identity. The RNA methyl group is not an encoded methylation-specific sequence change; the enrichment association carries the methylation evidence.

states.label: Sequence reads from the enriched RNA-derived library
features: This is the catalogue-described continuation beyond the image endpoint. The sequenced carrier is DNA derived from enriched RNA; reads identify the source RNA fragments.

The MeRIP full text interprets clustered reads as methylation-enriched RNA regions and compares them with non-IP input RNA. That control is reported in the paper, not drawn as a branch in this schematic.

The original MeRIP paper reports regional resolution of about 200 nt and notes that a peak can contain several m6A residues. These reads alone do not identify each methylated nucleotide or its methylation stoichiometry. This numerical resolution is not assigned to every implementation.

operations.label: Fractionate RNA
operations.description: The long RNA becomes a pool of shorter RNA fragments, including marked and unmarked pieces. The retained source caption is Fractionate RNA; the physical change is interpreted as fragmentation before antibody enrichment, as explicitly reported for MeRIP-Seq.
operations.mechanism: RNA fragmentation; the schematic does not establish a particular cleavage chemistry or terminal groups.
operations.information_effect: Fragmentation makes the selected and subsequently sequenced material a local segment of an RNA molecule; a captured fragment can contain the targeted mark anywhere along its length.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate
operations.description: The mixed RNA-fragment pool is exposed to m6A-directed antibodies. Red-marked fragments are depicted attached to pink antibodies, followed by a retained RNA population enriched for marked fragments. Antibody association and recovery are encompassed by this one broad block; no separate elution step or flow-through branch is drawn.
operations.mechanism: Antibody-mediated affinity enrichment of RNA bearing the targeted modification. The pink antibodies function as selection reagents. The MeRIP primary paper reports antibody-coupled beads and recovery of RNA; those interfaces are not separately drawn here.
operations.information_effect: Selection links the identity of retained RNA fragments to recognition by the antibody. Unmarked pieces are absent from the illustrated retained stream, but actual specificity remains antibody-dependent.

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: The selected purple RNA fragments are copied into black cDNA strands, changing the readout carrier from RNA to DNA. The RNA modification is represented indirectly through selection of its containing fragment.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated cDNA synthesis, as labeled by the diagram and stated by the catalogue; no particular enzyme, priming scheme, or strand chemistry is supplied.
operations.information_effect: The sequence of enriched RNA fragments is represented in cDNA. Methylation itself does not provide a distinguishing standard sequence call, so the antibody-enrichment association is necessary to interpret the reads.

method_scopes.rationale: The card explicitly associates MeRIP-Seq with Meyer et al. (PMID 22608085). Full text establishes fragmentation before RNA immunoprecipitation, enriched-RNA sequencing-library preparation, and regional methylation readout; the diagram/catalogue explicitly supply extraction and reverse transcription. The paper implements two rounds of capture within the single broad immunoprecipitation stage. One drawn block is not a count of capture rounds. The graph describes the explanatory architecture, not every step of that implementation.

method_scopes.rationale: The card associates this name with Dominissini et al. (PMID 22575960). Only its abstract is supplied: antibody-mediated capture and massively parallel sequencing are established, so these shared purposes are associated with the capture and sequencing records. The diagram groups the name with MeRIP-Seq, but extraction, fragmentation, reverse-transcription order, and the cDNA/library interface are not independently established for the Dominissini implementation by this abstract. op_sequence applies here only at the reported sequencing-purpose level; its detailed input carrier remains part of the family depiction. The two method names are not asserted to be exact protocol aliases.
